identity.title: Source Range Nuclear Instrument Failure Resulting in Condition Prohibited by Technical Specifications

cause.proximate_text: The direct cause of the source range neutron flux monitor failure was a failed power supply [JX]. The primary cause of the failure to identify the inoperable source range neutron flux monitor was the failure of the local indication light on the source range neutron flux monitor cabinet and the failure of the control room annunciator.
cause.theme: Instrument power supply failure combined with failed local/annunciator indication masking the loss of nuclear instrumentation during core reload

nodes.theme: Instrument power supply failure combined with failed local/annunciator indication masking the loss of nuclear instrumentation during core reload

nodes.display_name: Local indication light on source range neutron flux monitor cabinet

nodes.description: Power supply [JX] for the source range neutron flux monitor failed.
Source range neutron flux monitor failed low and was not responding as expected.
Local indication light on source range neutron flux monitor cabinet failed to provide reliable status; cause unknown, under investigation.
Control room annunciator failed to alarm as designed; cause unknown, under investigation.

nodes.display_name: Inoperable monitor not identified during fuel movement
nodes.description: Failure of local light and annunciator to alert operators meant the inoperable source range monitor was not identified while fuel assemblies were moved during core reload.

nodes.display_name: TS 3.9.2 LCO entered; condition prohibited by Technical Specifications (fuel movement with one required source range monitor inoperable)
Replace failed power supply and verify SRM operability
Revise core reload prerequisite check procedure to identify voltage issues with both source range monitors
Investigate and resolve local indication light and annunciator failures
Add procedure step for control room staff to monitor Plant Data Server points during core reload

ANO-1 LER 2005-002-00: Movement of Irradiated Fuel Assemblies with one Channel of Source Range Instrumentation Inoperable due to a Power Supply Failure Resulted in Operation Prohibited by Technical Specifications
nodes.title: Movement of Irradiated Fuel Assemblies with one Channel of Source Range Instrumentation Inoperable due to a Power Supply Failure Resulted in Operation Prohibited by Technical Specifications

chain: power supply [JX] fails [cause X] -> source range neutron flux monitor fails low -> (in parallel: local indication light fails; control room annunciator fails to alarm) -> inoperable monitor not identified during fuel movement -> fuel assemblies moved with one required source range monitor inoperable -> TS 3.9.2 LCO / condition prohibited by Technical Specifications
notes: Cause code X ('Other') is used because the RO/CAP had not yet determined why the local light and annunciator failed to function; direct cause (power supply failure) is clear but the primary/contributing causes remain under investigation, consistent with an 'Other/undetermined' categorization. The local light failure and annunciator failure are modeled as two separate parallel FailureModes since the narrative explicitly distinguishes them ('failure of the local indication light ... and the failure of the control room annunciator'). No BACKED_UP_BY edge emitted: while one of the two required source range monitors remained operable and monitored count rate, this is described as a safety-significance mitigating factor rather than a system/backup that was 'BACKED_UP_BY' in the causal-chain sense of an ECCS-style backup system substituting for a failed train; however, per rule 6 ambiguity, omitted rather than asserted incorrectly. Boron concentration and administrative suspension of core alterations were mitigating actions, not modeled as CorrectiveAction (they were immediate operator actions, not a corrective action program item) but the actual repair/replacement/procedure revisions are captured as CorrectiveAction nodes. Previous LER key preserved exactly as stated: '1-2005-002-00' reflecting the leading unit digit convention from the referenced ADAMS record (ANO-1 LER 2005-002-00).
